steps.user_message: I need to prepare internal financial materials. Our company Stellar Labs has $5.2M cash, 14 months runway, burn rate $45K/month, and revenue last quarter $3.2M. Can you help me with customer acquisition cost and LTV? I need to get the finance narrative right.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with finance-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Thanks — I can help. First, two quick checks and then a clear, repeatable way to compute CAC and LTV, some scenario examples, recommended targets, and a short finance narrative you can use in internal materials.

1) Immediate data inconsistency to resolve
- You told me: cash = $5.2M, runway = 14 months, burn = $45K/month.
- Those three cannot all be true at once:
  - If burn = $45K/month then runway = 5.2M / 45K ≈ 115.6 months (~9.6 years).
  - If runway = 14 months then implied burn = 5.2M / 14 ≈ $371,428/month.
Please confirm which monthly burn number is correct (raw cash outflow) and whether runway is computed from that burn. Also confirm whether the $45K is net burn after some adjustments (e.g., one-off items, capitalized expenses) or something else.

2) What I need from you to compute CAC and LTV precisely
- Sales & Marketing spend over the period you want to use for CAC (quarterly or annual S&M spend).
- Number of new customers acquired during that same period.
- Total number of customers (or customers by cohort), or at least ARPU (average revenue per customer) in the period.
- Gross margin (or contribution margin) percentage (revenue minus direct cost of goods sold, divided by revenue).
- Churn rate (preferably monthly churn or annual churn) or average customer lifetime.
If you don’t have all of these, I can run scenarios using reasonable assumptions — see examples below.

3) Formulas (simple, standard)
- CAC = Total Sales & Marketing spend over period / Number of new customers acquired in that period
- ARPU (monthly) = Total revenue in period / number of customers in that period, or monthly ARPU = (quarterly revenue / 3) / customers
- LTV (simplified) = ARPU per period × gross margin % × average customer lifetime (in same time units)
  - If you use churn rate (periodic), average lifetime (in periods) ≈ 1 / churn_rate
  - So LTV = ARPU_per_period × gross_margin × (1 / churn_rate)
- CAC payback (months) = CAC / (ARPU_monthly × gross_margin)

4) Quick numbers from what you gave (for orientation)
- Quarterly revenue = $3.2M → monthly revenue ≈ $1.067M.
- If you have N customers, monthly ARPU = $1.067M / N.
- Example: if you have 200 customers → monthly ARPU ≈ $5,333; annual ARPU ≈ $64k.

5) Example scenarios (three-statement examples you can copy into a slide)

Assumptions shown per scenario, outputs underneath. (Change any inputs with your real numbers.)

Scenario A — Conservative
- New customers last quarter: 10
- S&M spend that quarter: $800K
- Total customers: 200
- Gross margin: 70%
- Annual churn: 20% → average lifetime ≈ 5 years
Calculations:
- CAC = 800K / 10 = $80,000
- Monthly ARPU = (3.2M / 3) / 200 = $1,067,000 / 200 ≈ $5,335
- Annual ARPU ≈ $64,020
- LTV = Annual ARPU × GM × lifetime = 64,020 × 0.7 × 5 ≈ $224,070
- LTV:CAC ≈ 224,070 / 80,000 ≈ 2.8 (just below target)
- CAC payback months = 80,000 / (5,335 × 0.7) ≈ 21.5 months

Scenario B — Base
- New customers last quarter: 20
- S&M spend that quarter: $600K
- Total customers: 400
- Gross margin: 75%
- Annual churn: 15% → lifetime ≈ 6.67 years
Calculations:
- CAC = 600K / 20 = $30,000
- Monthly ARPU = 1,067,000 / 400 ≈ $2,668
- Annual ARPU ≈ $32,016
- LTV = 32,016 × 0.75 × 6.67 ≈ $160,020
- LTV:CAC ≈ 160,020 / 30,000 ≈ 5.3 (healthy)
- CAC payback months = 30,000 / (2,668 × 0.75) ≈ 15 months

Scenario C — Aggressive/Best
- New customers last quarter: 50
- S&M spend that quarter: $500K
- Total customers: 1,000
- Gross margin: 80%
- Annual churn: 10% → lifetime ≈ 10 years
Calculations:
- CAC = 500K / 50 = $10,000
- Monthly ARPU = 1,067,000 / 1,000 ≈ $1,067
- Annual ARPU ≈ $12,804
- LTV = 12,804 × 0.8 × 10 ≈ $102,432
- LTV:CAC ≈ 102,432 / 10,000 ≈ 10.2 (very strong)
- CAC payback months = 10,000 / (1,067 × 0.8) ≈ 11.7 months

Use these scenarios to see sensitivity to: new customer count, S&M spend, gross margin, and churn.

6) Targets and rules of thumb to include in your finance narrative
- Target LTV:CAC >= 3 (ideally 3–5 for SaaS / recurring revenue); >3 generally indicates healthy unit economics.
- CAC payback <= 12 months is a common investor comfort threshold; <18 months can be acceptable depending on growth stage.
- Higher gross margin and lower churn multiply LTV — retention is often higher ROI than acquisition.
- If you need to conserve cash or extend runway, prioritize reducing payback period and lowering CAC.
- Report cohort-based CAC and LTV (acquisition cohort by month/quarter) — it shows whether improvements are sustainable.

7) How to present this in the finance narrative (short paragraph + bullets you can paste)
Suggested one-paragraph narrative:
- “Stellar Labs finished last quarter with $3.2M revenue and $5.2M cash. Our current unit economics show that LTV/CAC is [insert computed ratio], with CAC payback of [insert months]. Key drivers are gross margin ([insert %]) and retention (annual churn [insert %]). We are targeting an LTV:CAC of ≥3 and a payback ≤12 months. To achieve this, we will (1) optimize channels with high conversion and lower CAC, (2) invest selectively in retention programs to increase LTV, and (3) monitor cohort CAC payback monthly to prioritize channels that meet our payback threshold.”

Accompany with bullets:
- Current cash runway: [insert confirmed months after you confirm burn]
- Key focus: reduce CAC or increase retention to improve LTV:CAC and shorten payback
- Actions: A/B test top 3 acquisition channels, pilot a 90-day onboarding/PS program to boost retention by X%, reduce spend on channels with >Y month payback.

8) Next steps I can do for you
- If you provide: S&M spend (quarterly or yearly), new customers added, total customers, gross margin, and churn — I will compute exact CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, and payback months and produce a one-page slide/text you can use in your deck.
- Or tell me which scenario of the three above you want refined and I’ll run sensitivity tables and a recommended narrative slide.

Which would you like next — (A) I run exact calculations if you provide the missing numbers (S&M spend, new customers, gross margin, churn), or (B) I build a short slide-ready narrative and sensitivity table using the scenario that most closely matches Stellar Labs?
